26.10.18.title: Numbers in your style
26.10.18.blurb: Settings has a Number format choice. Space and comma with Group digits shows this sheet's results as 1 234,5 and 15 431,2, while the source keeps its decimal points; in Input mode the load box takes 6,5 typed with a comma.

26.10.18.title: Menus in another language
26.10.18.blurb: The Language section at the top of Settings switches the interface at once. Choosing Deutsch turns the Settings dialog and the ribbon German, and choosing English switches them back.

26.10.18.title: Interactive panels
26.10.18.blurb: The Beam deflection explorer sample asks before it runs Python, then draws sliders and a drop-down in the results. Moving the span to 10 m and choosing Bending moment redraws the chart and the table in place, without recalculating the sheet.

26.10.17.title: A calculator for any page
26.10.17.blurb: Adding ?embed=1&sample= and a sample's id to the app address shows that sample as a compact form beside its results, ready for an iframe. Dragging the span from 6 m to 9 m works the moment out again and both checks change to fail.

26.10.15.title: Diagrams menu on the ribbon
26.10.15.blurb: The Plots tab is now Plots & Diagrams. Its Diagrams button, in the new Figures group, lists starter diagrams of each common engineering kind; here Flowchart inserts a design check as its own block, drawn in the results and ready to edit, and Undo takes it out again.

26.10.15.title: Samples that pair a diagram with the numbers
26.10.15.blurb: The Samples dialog opens the new Gable frame thrust sheet, with its decision diagram beside the pinned and rigid ridge calculations, and then the Sankey sheet that traces the power through a pump.

26.10.15.title: A ribbon that follows the work
26.10.15.blurb: Calculation now sits straight after Matrices/Tables, then Plots & Diagrams, Text Formatting, Document and Resources. Each tab's groups are regrouped to match, such as Check on Calculation and View, Panels and Help on Resources.

26.10.13.title: Block menu behind the grip
26.10.13.blurb: Hover a block of a sheet and a grip shows at its left. Its menu moves, duplicates, copies or deletes the block; here a line is duplicated, another moved down, and the toast at the bottom undoes the move.

26.10.13.title: Fold sections and drag blocks
26.10.13.blurb: The arrow under a heading's grip folds its section away and opens it again. Drag a grip to move a block; a heading takes its whole section along, and Undo puts it back.

26.10.13.title: Text toolbar and name completion
26.10.13.blurb: Select words in a paragraph opened in place and a small toolbar floats over them: here Bold, then a bulleted list. On a math line, typing a letter offers the names defined above it.

26.10.13.title: A slider on an input
26.10.13.blurb: Write a range in square brackets after an input's value, as in L: ? 6 m [2 .. 12 step 0.5] | span, and Input mode shows a slider beside its box. Drag it and the moment below is worked out again for each new span.

26.10.13.title: Diagrams drawn from text
26.10.13.blurb: A fenced block tagged mermaid is drawn as a diagram in the results, with the calculation under it. Here a new step typed into its text adds a box and an arrow back to the moment check.

26.10.13.title: Quick convert to a formula
26.10.13.blurb: Select an expression in a line of text, here w*L^2/8, and press = Formula on the toolbar or Ctrl+Shift+E. It becomes a formula line after the paragraph with its name selected; typing Mmid names it and the preview works out 54 kN m.

26.10.13.title: Sort a table by a column
26.10.13.blurb: Click a column heading of a table in the results to sort by it. Here Load sorts ascending, then descending, and a third click puts the rows back in the order of the source, which is never changed.

26.10.12.title: Templates with inputs
26.10.12.blurb: Open a template from the Samples dialog and switch to Input mode. Here the soil in a pad footing check is changed from medium dense sand to soft clay, and the verdict at the bottom of the page changes from OK to Fails.

26.10.12.title: An input is one line of a sheet
26.10.12.blurb: Start the value of a sheet line with a question mark, as in L: ? 6 m | span, and Input mode shows a number box for it with its unit. Everything below that uses L follows what is typed in the box.

26.10.12.title: On-screen math keyboard
26.10.12.blurb: The Keyboard item in the status bar opens a math keyboard, a panel you can drag on a desktop. Here a few clicks type y = 2 × π and the sheet calculates it.

26.10.12.title: Insert strip between blocks
26.10.12.blurb: Hover between two rendered blocks of a sheet and a + appears. It opens a menu of blocks to insert at that place; here a table goes in under the heading, with its first cell selected ready to type over.

26.10.12.title: Plot chips: log axes and save as PNG
26.10.12.blurb: Under each plot in the preview a row of chips switches an axis to a log scale, makes the axes 1:1, copies the data and saves the plot as PNG or SVG. This one turns both axes to log, then saves a PNG.

26.10.12.title: Edit in place
26.10.12.blurb: One click on a block of a sheet opens it where it stands. Click away and the change is applied; Esc throws it away.

26.10.11.title: Plots sample
26.10.11.blurb: The Plots sample is a gallery of Plotly plots with implicit curves, functions, polylines and a second y axis. Here the results pane scrolls through the first of them and back.

26.10.10.title: Phone layout
26.10.10.blurb: On a screen 760 px wide or less the app shows one pane at a time, switched from a bar along the bottom: Edit, Results and Insert.

26.10.9.title: Symbolic dialog
26.10.9.blurb: The Symbolic button on the Functions tab opens a small computer algebra dialog. Here the bending moment w*x^2/2 of a cantilever is integrated from 0 to L, the answer is typeset, and Insert into worksheet adds it to the sheet as a formula block.

26.10.8.title: Rich-text editing in place
26.10.8.blurb: Double-click a paragraph of a sheet and it opens as a text editor where it stands. Here one word is made bold with the B button, a click outside applies the change, and the paragraph is written back as Markdown.

26.10.7.title: Python is coloured
26.10.7.blurb: A Python block in a sheet is coloured with the Python grammar while you type: keywords, numbers, strings and comments each get their own colour, and the rest of the sheet keeps its own colours.

26.10.6.title: Plotly charts from Python
26.10.6.blurb: The Beam Explorer sample solves a three-span beam in Python and draws it with the Plotly API, no HTML or JavaScript. Plotly's own menu picks the load case, here one span loaded and then all spans again.

26.10.5.title: Plane truss in Python
26.10.5.blurb: The Plane Truss by the Stiffness Method sample assembles a truss in loops and solves it with numpy.linalg in the page. The preview shows the member forces and reactions, then the Calcpad lines that use the exported values.

26.10.4.title: Python values used by later lines
26.10.4.blurb: A Python block in a sheet computes a moment and hands it back with export(M_py=M). The line after the block uses M_py, so changing L in the Python from 6 to 8 changes the design moment below it.

26.10.3.title: Sheets: name, expression, unit, note
26.10.3.blurb: In a sheet each line is name: expression -> unit | note. Two lines are typed and the preview typesets them with their units, then the Samples dialog shows its group of sheet samples.

26.10.1.title: Samples browser and dark theme
26.10.1.blurb: The Samples browser opens one of the bundled worksheets, grouped by topic. The Dark button on the Resources tab then switches the preview to the dark theme, and Light switches it back.

26.10.1.title: Word export
26.10.1.blurb: File, Export opens the export dialog. Save Word writes the report as a Word file in the page, with no server involved; here the download starts and the dialog is closed.
